content: Nelfinavir affects the metabolism of various drugs by interacting with hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, and other transporters like P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Below are the detailed interactions and clinical considerations for co-administration: 1. Nelfinavir and Pramlintide: Nelfinavir decreases the effects of pramlintide. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Nelfinavir and Pravastatin: Nelfinavir increases the toxicity of pravastatin. OATP1B1 inhibitors may elevate the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 3. Nelfinavir and Praziquantel: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Nelfinavir and Prednisolone/Prednisone: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 5. Primidone and Nelfinavir: Primidone decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Quercetin and Nelfinavir: Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir through P-glycoprotein efflux. Use caution and monitor. 7. Nelfinavir and Quetiapine: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 8. Nelfinavir and Quinidine: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin and Nelfinavir: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Nelfinavir and Quizartinib: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Ranolazine and Nelfinavir: Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir through P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 12. Nelfinavir and Repaglinide: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 13. Ribociclib and Nelfinavir: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifapentine and Nelfinavir: Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Nelfinavir and Rifaximin: Nelfinavir increases the levels of rifaximin through P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 16. Nelfinavir and Rilpivirine: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of rilpivirine via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 17. Nelfinavir and Ripretinib: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite, DP-5439, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 18. Nelfinavir and Ritonavir: Nelfinavir and ritonavir mutually increase each other's levels or effects via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein interactions. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 19. Nelfinavir and Rivaroxaban: Nelfinavir increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, significantly increasing bleeding risk. Avoid concomitant use with combined P-glycoprotein and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Nelfinavir and Roflumilast (Topical): Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of roflumilast via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 21. Nelfinavir and Rosiglitazone: Nelfinavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 22. Rucaparib and Nelfinavir: Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Rufinamide and Nelfinavir: Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Nelfinavir and Sacubitril/Valsartan: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of valsartan via OATP1B1 inhibition. Co-administration may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 25. Nelfinavir and Saxagliptin: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Nelfinavir and Seladelpar: Nelfinavir increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Nelfinavir and Sertraline: Nelfinavir increases sertraline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 28. Sirolimus and Nelfinavir: Sirolimus increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 29. Nelfinavir and Sitagliptin: Nelfinavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin. Reports suggest hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 30. Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate and Nelfinavir: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Nelfinavir and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 32. Nelfinavir and Solifenacin: Nelfinavir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 33. Nelfinavir and Sorafenib: Nelfinavir increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 34. Sparsentan and Nelfinavir: Sparsentan decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 35. St. John’s Wort and Nelfinavir: St. John’s Wort decreases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Use caution and monitor. 36. Stiripentol and Nelfinavir: Stiripentol increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 37. Nelfinavir and Sufentanil SL: Nelfinavir increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. 38. Nelfinavir and Sunitinib: Nelfinavir increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 39. Nelfinavir and Tacrolimus: Nelfinavir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Tacrolimus also increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 40. Nelfinavir and Tasimelteon: Nelfinavir increases tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 41. Tazemetostat and Nelfinavir: Tazemetostat decreases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 42. Tecovirimat and Nelfinavir: Tecovirimat increases nelfinavir levels via CYP2C19 inhibition but decreases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness. 43. Nelfinavir and Temsirolimus: Nelfinavir increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 44. Nelfinavir and Teniposide: Nelfinavir increases teniposide levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 45. Nelfinavir and Tenofovir DF: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 46. Nelfinavir and Terbinafine: Nelfinavir increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 47. Nelfinavir and Tezacaftor: Nelfinavir increases tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 48. Nelfinavir and Theophylline: Nelfinavir increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 49. Nelfinavir and Ticagrelor: Nelfinavir increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 50. Nelfinavir and Tinidazole: Nelfinavir increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 51. Nelfinavir and Tipranavir: Nelfinavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 52. Nelfinavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Nelfinavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for adverse effects. 53. Nelfinavir and Tolterodine: Nelfinavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 54. Tolvaptan and Nelfinavir: Tolvaptan increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 55. Topiramate and Nelfinavir: Topiramate decreases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor. 56. Nelfinavir and Toremifene: Nelfinavir increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 57. Nelfinavir and Tramadol: Nelfinavir increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 58. Nelfinavir and Trazodone: Nelfinavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while trazodone decreases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Use caution and monitor. 59. Nelfinavir and Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension: Nelfinavir increases triamcinolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 60. Nelfinavir and Triazolam: Nelfinavir increases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 61. Triclabendazole and Nelfinavir: Triclabendazole increases nelfinavir levels via CYP2C19 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 62. Nelfinavir and Trimipramine: Nelfinavir increases trimipramine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 63. Tucatinib and Nelfinavir: Tucatinib increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Consider reducing the dosage of P-glycoprotein substrates if adverse reactions occur. 64. Ublituximab and Nelfinavir: Ublituximab decreases nelfinavir effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 65. Nelfinavir and Ulipristal: Nelfinavir increases ulipristal levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 66. Nelfinavir and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol Inhaled: Nelfinavir increases vilanterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 67. Nelfinavir and Upadacitinib: Nelfinavir increases upadacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 68. Nelfinavir and Valbenazine: Nelfinavir increases valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 69. Nelfinavir and Valsartan: Nelfinavir increases valsartan levels via OATP1B1 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 70. Nelfinavir and Vamorolone: Nelfinavir increases vamorolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients >50 kg. 71. Nelfinavir and Vardenafil: Nelfinavir increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce vardenafil dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
